entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Neeraj Singh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anit Kumar Shukla, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.176 of 2024, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506, 376 I.P.C. & 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Deoranian, District Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.

4. The instant case is a matrimonial matter between the families and the applicant, who happens to be the brother-in-law (jeth) of the victim, is stated to have committed sexual assault and unnatural offence with the victim for a substantial period of time.
Rashid vs State Of U.P. on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151885713/
1 5.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The allegations are per se false.
There is no medical corroboration of the said incident.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.

The circumstances which,
as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 17.07.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. The Supreme Court in the judgment of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar,
2022(6) SCC 599 has categorically opined that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text:
Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar,
2022(6) SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

8. The Supreme Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785 has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant-Rashid, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

Rashid vs State Of U.P. on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151885713/
2 11.

In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
12.

It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 6.2.2025 (Ravi Kant) (Justice Krishan Pahal)
